cards.note:
A-Type with yellow reflectors

NOTE: Within Europe, yellow reflectors are only found in Andorra, Spain and Belgium

Belgium uses A-type guardrails with yellow reflectors.

NOTE: In Europe, only Spain, Andorra, and Belgium use these reflectors.

Guardrails sometimes feature yellow and black markings. These markings always have the yellow stripes on the outside.

NOTE: Peru has similar markings. However, in Peru, the markings have the inverse colour scheme: the black stripes are always on the outside.
British Columbia predominantly uses concrete barriers instead of guardrails.
In Newfoundland and Labrador, most wooden posts on guardrails have this pyramid shaped top. Occasionally, you can spot them on standalone posts and signposts as well.
In Ontario, you will often see these types of guardrails. They consist of cylindrical wooden posts, held together by precisely three metal wires. Some posts are marked by a reflective white band.

cards.a: Czechoslovakia  - Unique Thin B-Type with red reflectors
cards.note:
Czechia and Slovakia both use a special kind of type B guardrail, which is wider than the normal type. No other European countries use the same kind.

NOTE: While Slovakia occasionally uses other types of guardrails, Czechia is fairly consistent.

Denmark has square (normal B-type) guardrails, with no reflectors.

NOTE: Denmark is one of only a very few European countries with this type of guardrail.

cards.a: Eastern Europe  - A-Type with red reflectors
cards.note:
In most eastern european countries you have an A-Type guardrail with (mainly) red reflectors, so I decided to group them. The countries following this rule are: Austria, Slovenia, Hungary, Albania, Greece, North Macedonia, Romania, Bulgaria, Ukraine and Russia. The countries with the less seen B-Type guardrail in eastern europe are Poland, Croatia, Serbia and Montenegro (which has A-Type & B-Type).

Check the infographic for more detail!

cards.a: Eastern Europe  - B-Type with red reflectors
cards.note:
In a few eastern european countries you have an B-Type guardrail with (mainly) red reflectors and I decided to group them. The countries with the B-Type guardrail in eastern europe are Poland, Croatia, Serbia and Montenegro (which has A-Type & B-Type).

Check the infographic for more detail!
Double guardrails are very commonly used. This is much less common in other South American countries.

Estonia has normal A-type guardrails with no reflectors.

NOTE: The other two Baltic countries can have reflectors on their guardrails.

France uses A-type guardrails, usually without reflectors. On rare occasions, you can find thin B-type, the standard guardrail in Czechia and Slovakia.

NOTE: Spanish, Andorran and Belgian guardrails use yellow reflectors. Luxembourg has an A-Type guardrail with white reflectors aswell-

cards.a: Germany  -  A or B-Type w/o reflectors
cards.note:
While most of Germany uses B-Type guardrails, some regions predominantly use A-Type instead. Learning which regions use them can be useful.

NOTE: There will always be rare exceptions.

Ireland uses (just like Germany) A & B-Type guardrails without any reflectors.

NOTE: The UK only uses A-Type guardrails.

cards.a: Italy  -  A-Type with orange or red reflectors
cards.note:
Italian guardrails feature orange or red front reflectors. Also, they often are doubled, just like in Ecuador.

NOTE: This is most useful to distinguish Italy from Spain, which uses yellow reflectors. For a good overview of European guardrails, see this infographic.
Italian guardrails commonly end in this distinct shape. The guardrail gets flatter, wider, and it bends away from the road.
These distinctive yellow guardrails can be found in the Yamaguchi Prefecture.

cards.a: Latvia  -  A-Type with red or white reflectors
cards.note:
Latvia has normal A-type guardrails with white or red reflectors.

NOTE: Estonia has no reflectors. Lithuania has orange reflectors.

Lithuania has normal A-type guardrails with orange reflectors.

NOTE: Estonia has no reflectors. Latvia has red or white reflectors.

cards.a: Montenegro  -  (Rusty) A & B-Type with red reflectors
cards.note: Montenegro is the only Balkan country where you’ll commonly see both A-type and B-type guardrails. Guardrails in Montenegro are often rusted.

Norway uses A-Type guardrails. Guardrails often have wooden posts.

NOTE: This is not common in Sweden or Finland.

Black-and-yellow stripes on guardrails are seen throughout the country. You might sometimes find different designs, such as this sharp arrow design.

NOTE: Similar striped guardrails are also found in Bolivia. To differentiate them, just have a look at the outer stripe. Peru uses a black one, while Bolivia features a yellow one.

Portugal uses A-type guardrails with red reflectors.

NOTE: This is mostly useful to tell apart Portugal and Spain, which uses yellow reflectors.

Spain has yellow reflectors on rounded A-type guardrails.

NOTE: Belgium, Andorra and Gibraltar also have yellow reflectors. For a good overview of European guardrails, see this infographic.

cards.a: Switzerland & Netherlands  - Switzerland & Netherlands - A-Type w/o reflectors
cards.note: Switzerland and Netherlands both have regular A-Type guardrails. Most of their neighbors do have reflectors so it can be quite good to know.

cards.a: Turkey  - A & B-Type with red reflectors
cards.note:
Turkey uses both main types of guardrails:

A-type guardrails, which have rounded edges.

B-type guardrails, which have square edges.

While most Mediterranean countries use the A-type, B-type can help solve some tough 50-50s. Furthermore, seeing both types will exclude all southern European and Middle Eastern countries, other than Montenegro and Israel & the West Bank.

UK only use A-Type guardrails which makes it useful to differentiate between Ireland and the UK.

NOTE: Ireland uses both A & B-Type.

Guardrails, signs, and signposts are commonly painted a medium brown colour in US National Parks, which are often located in the west. Guardrails that are painted brown can be made out of both wood and metal. Rock walls can also sometimes be seen in place of guardrails.

Here you can find a map showing where all US National Parks are located.

NOTE: There are occasional exceptions to this rule, so consider other clues before guessing in a National Park.

Square guardrails are the most dominant (but not the only) type of guardrail in the states of New York and Wyoming. They have a long bar across the top, with several square legs supporting them.

NOTE: These guardrails can be found, to a lesser extent, in some adjacent states.
